_note: Every value here is either a published figure (type=fact, with source) or a modelling assumption (type=assumption, with a range used in sensitivity and Monte Carlo runs). Change a value and re-run `python -m wattwage.build`.

monthly_seasonality.how: Relative to the annual monthly mean (averages to 1.0). Typical Saudi residential load shape: summer cooling roughly 3x winter.

consumption_lognormal_sigma.how: Spread of monthly household consumption around the mean

breaker_mix.how: Share of residential accounts by breaker size; SEC does not publish this split

price_elasticity_short_run.source: KAPSARC (2020): short-run residential elasticity about -0.1 after the 2018 reform; residential use fell 9.1%

water_litres_per_capita_day.how: Commonly cited Saudi residential per-capita use; household size 5.5

cpi_weight_electricity_pct.how: Residential electricity spending (~30 bn SAR + 15% VAT) / private consumption (~1.65 tn SAR, CEIC 2024). GASTAT does not publish the sub-group weight in the sources used.

cpi_weight_water_pct.how: Low end: ~9.2m accounts x ~30 SAR/month / private consumption; high end: the simulated average water bill (~1,700 SAR/year) x 9.2m / private consumption. Many flats share one meter, so the true weight sits between.

indirect_passthrough_ratio.how: Second-round effect from higher commercial, industrial and government tariffs, as a share of the direct household effect

baseline_cpi_window_start.how: Post-VAT regime used to fit the no-reform baseline

support_2018_cost_bn_sar_year.source: Al-Jarida (7 Jan 2018), citing Saudi officials: 1,000 SAR employees, 500 SAR retirees and social security

beneficiaries_million.how: Calibrated so the 2018 package (1,000/500/500 SAR) costs about 50 bn SAR a year; government sector workers in GOSI = 1.139m (NLO Q2 2026) plus military

gosi_employer_rate_saudi_pct.source: setupinsaudi.com summary of GOSI rates from 1 Jul 2026

nitaqat_phase1_date.how: Six months after the measures start; start read as the decision date (alt: tariff start date)
